sample_unit: MIMIC-IV patients with synthetically injected PII (plus other multimodal datasets)

links.outcome: Deidentification sensitivity of the multi-agent system across multimodal benchmark datasets
links.effect: Best local configuration reached per-patient sensitivity 98.80% (95%-CI 97.20; 100) and per-PII sensitivity 99.82% (95%-CI 99.76; 99.88), with critical clinical preservation 99.60% per-patient.
links.quote: The best local configuration—the orchestrator being Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking—achieved near-complete deidentification across all datasets, with per-patient sensitivity of 98.80% (95%-CI 97.20; 100), and per-PII sensitivity of 99.82% (95%-CI 99.76; 99.88).

unlisted_practices: fully local on-premises multi-agent deidentification of multimodal clinical data
preservation of clinically important content during deidentification
iterative verification within multi-agent deidentification pipeline

screen.reason: The paper introduces and benchmarks a novel multi-agent multimodal de-identification tool (Multimodal Anonymizer) on synthetic and retrospective clinical datasets. While de-identification is relevant to data privacy, this study focuses on the development and benchmark evaluation of the new AI system itself rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
